data.title: Fed Officials Signal December Rate Increase Remains on Track — WSJ
data.description:
By Nick Timiraos

Three Federal Reserve officials on Friday signaled support for continuing to raise interest rates, most likely at the central bank's next meeting in December, after having held them steady this week.

"Skipping a meeting does not change the monetary policy destination," said Dallas Fed President Lorie Logan, in remarks delivered to college students Friday that were released by the bank.

Logan voted in favor of the decision to hold steady this week. The last time the Fed held rates steady, in July, Logan dissented in favor of a rate increase. The Fed raised rates in September. Two of the 12 voting members of the Federal Open Market Committee dissented this week in favor of a rate increase.

Logan repeated her view that the Fed needs to make at least two more increases of a quarter point. She said moving gradually made sense after recent market swings and because the timing of any increase matters less if investors understand where the Fed is ultimately headed.

After making two additional rate increases, she said, "it would make sense in my view to pause and examine economic and financial developments to determine what further action may be appropriate."

St. Louis Fed President Alberto Musalem, who isn't a voter on policy this year, said he judged "additional firming of monetary policy will be necessary, and soon." Without further increases, he said inflation would likely stay well above the Fed's 2% target over the next 18 months.

During remarks in New York, Musalem spelled out what it would take to convince him to hold off. Inflation could ease without more Fed rate increases if energy prices and shipping costs fall. Demand could also slow more than expected if spending on the AI build-out drops sharply or if a sudden pullback in financial markets leads wealthier households to retrench. Musalem said he saw this scenario as "less likely but plausible."

Both officials signaled little concern about recent turbulence in financial markets. Logan said the run-up in long-term interest rates this year mostly reflects investors' expectations of stronger growth, a sign that "monetary policy has work to do."

Richmond Fed President Tom Barkin told Sirius XM Business Radio a "gradual approach" to raising rates made sense because the Fed is "not much behind the curve."

This item is part of a Wall Street Journal live coverage event. The full stream can be found by searching P/WSJL (WSJ Live Coverage).

data.title: META, AMZN, ORCL, GOOGL In Focus: Big Tech Bonds Offer Better Opportunity Than Stocks, BofA Says
data.description:
Key points:
  • Hyperscalers are currently offering bond yields between 6% and 8%, drawing investor attention away from volatile equities. 
  • Tech giants are grappling with unprecedented capital expenditures and negative free cash flows, with cumulative debt and equity issuance hitting $271 billion this year. 
  • Recent equity maneuvers—such as Meta’s $95 billion stock offering plan—signal that the historic era of aggressive corporate stock buybacks may be coming to a close. 

Bank of America guided investors toward mega-cap technology corporate bonds instead of equities as an investment opportunity. Michael Hartnett, chief investment strategist at BofA, noted that fixed-income instruments issued by the "Magnificent Seven" and other major tech players provide compelling value.

The surge in borrowing costs stems directly from escalating anxiety surrounding the massive capital expenditures made by hyperscalers like Meta (META), Google (GOOG, GOOGL), Amazon (AMZN), and Oracle (ORCL), among others, to build out generative artificial intelligence infrastructure.

As tech firms tap capital markets aggressively to fund these heavy digital expansions, BofA highlighted that the yields on investment-grade debt have climbed to attractive ranges between 6% and 8%.

Soaring Capex And Earnings Pressure

The pivot toward debt markets comes on the heels of a turbulent week for technology stocks. Following quarterly earnings reports, several major tech corporations revealed unexpectedly high negative free cash flows alongside staggering capital expenditures.

Industry giants continue to scale up investments exponentially, pushing projected annual capital expenditures. For instance, Google’s 2026 AI capex is expected to land in the $195 billion to $205 billion range. Even traditional holdouts are altering their financing strategies; Microsoft recently announced a $25 billion debt issuance to support its artificial intelligence initiatives. Across the sector, total debt and equity issuance by major hyperscalers has reached $271 billion for the year.

Implications For Shareholders 

While the debt market offers high yields—with Oracle leading investment-grade tech bonds above 8% and companies like Meta and Amazon offering yields between 6.8% and 7.4%—the equity landscape faces fresh headwinds.

Meta Platforms recently bucked the pure-debt trend by turning to equity financing, announcing plans to secure $95 billion via stock offerings.

According to Hartnett, expanded share issuance acts as a negative catalyst for existing equity holders and serves as an indicator that the prolonged era of massive corporate stock buybacks has likely drawn to a close.

META, GOOGL, AMZN, ORCL Stock: Retail View 

Retail view on Stocktwits was ‘bearish’ on Meta and ‘bullish’ on Google, Amazon and Oracle.

META stock has dropped 6%, GOOGL has lost about 10%, Amazon has gained 3%, and Oracle stock has lost about 33% year-to-date.

data.title: Block Deals: Tencent Holdings exits Swiggy for Rs 982 crore
data.description:
Chinese multinational technology conglomerate Tencent Holdings through its subsidiary exited Swiggy, the food delivery company, by selling entire shareholding for nearly Rs 982 crore via open market transactions on October 30.

Swiggy shares seem to have reacted to the block deals, falling 4.67 percent to end at Rs 176.6, near its record low levels. The fall was accompanied by above-average volumes.

Tencent Cloud Europe B V on Friday sold 5.43 crore equity shares, equivalent to 1.96 percent of paid-up equity, in Swiggy, for Rs 981.79 crore.

All the shares sold by Tencent in Swiggy were bought by global and domestic institutional investors at a price of Rs 180.65 apiece.

Aditya Birla Sun Life Mutual Fund acquired additional 14.92 lakh shares in Swiggy for Rs 26.95 crore. The asset management company through Aditya Birla Sun Life Value Fund already held 1.12 percent stake (3.08 crore shares) in the food delivery company as of September 2026.

Societe Generale bought 2.37 crore Swiggy shares for Rs 428.86 crore, while Nippon India Mutual Fund purchased 27.67 lakh shares for Rs 49.98 crore.

Ghisallo Master Fund LP acquired 26.08 lakh Swiggy shares for Rs 47.12 crore, while Goldman Sachs Bank Europe SE bought 1.05 crore shares for Rs 190.58 crore, and Morgan Stanley Asia Singapore picked up 1.31 crore shares for Rs 238.27 crore.

data.title: Walmart Invests in Texas Battery Company Base Power
data.description:
By Katherine Hamilton

Walmart has invested in Texas energy company Base Power as part of a strategic agreement.

Base Power installs, owns and maintains home battery systems, with customers paying an upfront installation fee. The systems are designed to cut energy costs when the grid is on and provide backup power when it isn't.

As part of the deal, Walmart would make Base's home energy offerings available to customers and Sam's Club members. Beginning in November, customers who enroll in eligible Base battery offerings would receive 20% off the standard upfront battery-installation fee.

Texas is Base's biggest and most established market. It serves 35,000 members in the state. Walmart is launching the offerings in Texas first and expects to expand to additional locations over time.

Write to Katherine Hamilton at katherine.hamilton@wsj.com

data.title: Gold Nosedives Amid Concerns Of Monetary Tightening, U.S.-Iran Standoff
data.description:
WASHINGTON (dpa-AFX) - Extending the downward move seen over the two previous sessions, gold prices went into freefall on Friday as rising crude oil prices due to the stalemate in the U.S.-Iran peace process increased inflation worries and reinforced concerns of rate hikes in the U.S. as well as other countries.

Front Month Comex Gold for December delivery has experienced a tailspin by $131.30 (or 3.26%) to $3,900.10 per troy ounce.

Front Month Comex Silver for December delivery has also nosedived by $3.170 (or 6.05%) to $49.210 per troy ounce.

The ongoing gulf crisis and supply shortage for oil and energy is driving crude oil up and pushing inflation concerns further. WTI crude oil for December delivery was last seen trading at $104.85, up by $2.85 (or 2.79%).

Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps announced that four tankers struck sea mines planted by Iran while attempting to transit the Strait of Hormuz and violating Iran-stipulated navigation protocol that Iran's military termed as 'illegal shipping lanes.'

In addition, days after senior officials from Saudi Arabia and Iran held talks in Tehran to address regional security and peace through dialogue, the Iran-backed Houthi militant group claimed nearly six attacks on airports and oil facilities across Saudi Arabia.

The threat of an increase in oil prices reinforced expectations of elevated interest rates globally for a prolonged period of time which will eventually make non-yielding assets like gold unattractive.

Reports since last week have indicated that the U.S. is planning to conduct strikes against Iran jointly with Israel after the midterm elections in the U.S. on November 3.

The attacks could be on a bigger scale than before with an aim to cripple Iran's capability to reconstitute and strike back.

The Wall Street Journal reported that U.S. Vice President JD Vance wrote to Iran's Secretary of the Supreme National Security Council Mohsen Rezaei, asking Iran to quickly return to peace talks.

Reportedly, Vance's efforts are aimed to persuade Trump to pause his planned attacks on Iran, showing that the peace process is moving on. The letter has been well-received by Iran.

Mediators from Qatar are headed to Iran again to push for a nuclear framework between the U.S. and Iran.

On Sunday, Qatar presented a draft proposal that reportedly Iran rejected as it stated that it fell short of Iran's expectations.

Without offering a response, Iran is maintaining silence, adding to tensions.

Yesterday, data from the U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis showed that the U.S. Gross Domestic Product increased 3.40% in Q3 2026. This is a sharp jump from the 2.20% growth in Q2 2026.

Consumer spending grew 3.80%, matching Q2 rate.

The U.S. Personal Consumption Expenditures price index increased 0.50% on a month-on-month basis for September. The annual inflation accelerated to 3.60%.

The Conference Board showed that consumer confidence is improving, despite inflation and increasing gas prices.

Through Truth Social U.S. President Donald Trump announced that the data was a major boost for the U.S. economy.

On Wednesday, the U.S. Federal Reserve decided to keep the interest rates steady at the prevailing 3.75% to 4.00%.

According to the CME Group's FedWatch Tool, traders are betting on a 74.40% chance for a rate hike at the December meeting of the Fed.

Following the Fed, the European Central Bank also held the rates steady.

The ECB hinted that tightening process is not yet over and could continue if energy costs push inflation higher.

Data from the Institute for Supply Management today revealed that Chicago Purchasing Managers' Index decreased to 55.30 in October from 58.80 in September.

Weakness in gold, according to analysts, is also due to forced liquidations linked to the equity selloff as investors tend to cover losses in equity markets by selling liquid assets.

data.title: Vail Resorts' biggest investor backs company in fight with activist Oasis
data.description:
By Svea Herbst-Bayliss

Vail Resorts won support on Friday from its largest investor as it faces increasing pressure from activist Oasis Management to make operational changes including the possible sale of some mountain assets.

Ron Baron said in a statement his firm Baron Capital, which owned 18% of Vail's stock at the end of June, will back Vail's management at next month's boardroom election and will vote for Vail Resorts' nominees.

Baron added that he believes Vail CEO Rob Katz "has the right strategy to return to sustainable earnings growth."

BOARDROOM FIGHT

Vail, which owns mountain resorts and ski areas in Utah, Colorado and the northeastern United States, is facing off against Oasis, an activist investor and Vail's fourth-biggest shareholder with a 9% stake at the end of September, in one of the year's most contentious boardroom fights.

Oasis wants changes, including the possible sale of some mountain assets, and in September nominated four director candidates, including former Olympic ski champion Picabo Street and former Walt Disney CEO Bob Chapek.

Vail, which has a market value of $5 billion, is urging investors to vote for its nine directors and argues its multi-year transformation strategy, dubbed "Epic Experience", will pay off. It has already made changes like upgrading its quick service menu items, improving ticket purchasing and offering advance purchase discounts. It has also upgraded its ski school and lessons.

'SHORT-SIGHTED' EFFORT

Since January, Vail's stock price has climbed 13% and is trading at $151.37 on Friday. But over the last five years, the stock tumbled nearly 50% and the company said last month that full fiscal-year profit nearly halved compared with a year earlier. Record low snowfall brought fewer guests to Vail's mountains and has weighed on earnings.

Baron also referenced a simmering fight around billionaire tech company Cloudflare Chief Executive Matthew Prince, who has been pushing to buy Park City Mountain Resort from Vail.

"I also have serious concerns about Oasis' coordination with Matthew Prince," Baron wrote, adding he views Prince's effort to have Vail sell him Park City as "short-sighted and destructive to long-term shareholder value."

A representative for Oasis said: "It's not surprising that the board would try to distract shareholders from their poor performance by making misleading statements — from false accusations about coordination to asserting that the board has done a great job. We continue to believe in the value of the assets and the need for board refreshment."

Prince could not be reached for comment.

data.title: Nasdaq Newcomer Sees Growth for Oil Well Logging Technology — Interview
data.description:
(17:47 GMT) *GOWell CEO Sees Solid Demand for Well Logging Technology
(17:47 GMT) *GOWell CEO: Nasdaq Listing Gives Visibility, Easier Access to Capital
(17:48 GMT) *GOWell CEO: Energy Security Concerns Support Need for Logging Technology
(17:48 GMT) Nasdaq Newcomer Sees Growth for Oil Well Logging Technology — Interview

By Anthony Harrup

Oil well logging technology company GOWell Energy Technology sees increasing demand for its equipment and expects its recent listing on Nasdaq to help in its bid to grow, according to the company's chief executive.

GOWell Energy Technology began trading on Nasdaq at the end of September following a business combination with Inflection Point Acquisition Corp. V, a special purpose acquisition company.

The company designs and manufactures equipment to monitor for leaks, corrosion, or other defects in wells. It doesn't provide field services, but oil-field services companies deploy its technology, CEO Guillaume Borrel said in an interview.

GOWell's latest technology stays within the tubing of a well and can see behind the outer casing without the need to remove the tubing, Borrel said. "That's massive savings and these are our innovations."

GOWell, with headquarters in Singapore and a principal office in Houston where it carries out its research and development, expects to see solid sales growth amid strong demand for well logging.

Its main operating subsidiary reported revenue of $33.8 million, a 43% increase over the first half of 2025, and for the full year expects revenue between $60 million and $68 million, up from $47.2 million in 2025.

Advantages of GOWell's decision to go public include greater visibility in the global marketplace and easier access to capital markets if needed for organic growth or to pursue acquisitions, Borrel said. "We do have an ambitious M&A program and plan."

Among the reasons for the optimism is the demand for well logging technology, particularly at a time when energy security is becoming of major importance, he said. That is driving focus on getting more out of existing infrastructure.

"The wells we have already in the ground, can we open them a bit more, can we squeeze a few more drops out? Can we go back into them and start them up again if they've been shut in?" Borrel said.

That requires well integrity.

"We need to make sure the hydrocarbon stays where it needs to be inside the tubing, and doesn't leak outside, or stuff on the outside doesn't leak inside," Borrel said. "Any operator tries to protect not just the environment but also the actual hydrocarbon they're producing."

Another source of demand for the technology is the decommissioning of wells that need to be properly plugged when they reach the end of their life cycle, he added.
